# Contribution and claim boundaries (TB-048)

*Generated by `scripts/build-report.py` from stored artifacts (numbers) and checked by `scripts/check-claims.py`: the project's
public text is scanned for novelty, security-guarantee, publication and résumé claims, and any that this register does not
allow fails the check. Inputs: the technical report [`report.md`](report.md) (TB-047) and the prior-work matrix
[`related-work.csv`](related-work.csv) (TB-043). This register has not been reviewed by a specialist; it supports no patent
or publication claim, and any such claim needs specialist review first.*

## Replicated or adapted from prior work

These ideas are not TrustBench's. The project implements or re-implements them and measures them on its own harness.

| Component | Prior work | What TrustBench did with it | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Per-call tool allowlists and argument contracts | Progent (RW22); tool filter (RW12) | Implemented in the capability gateway; with the gateway as a whole, the only components the development ablations credit | [`docs/ablations.md`](../docs/ablations.md) |
| Confirmation of consequential calls | RTBAS (RW21) | Exact-argument approval bound to normalised arguments; no measurable contribution in the development ablations | [`src/gateway/README.md`](../src/gateway/README.md), [`docs/ablations.md`](../docs/ablations.md) |
| Separating trusted control from untrusted data; capability-tracked values | CaMeL (RW19) | A simplified CaMeL-style agent, measured as a comparison system | [`docs/camel.md`](../docs/camel.md) |
| Provenance labels and integrity tracking of untrusted data | FIDES (RW20); CaMeL (RW19) | Signed provenance on tool outputs and a directive-flow check, as a narrower empirical form without a formal model | [`docs/flow-check.md`](../docs/flow-check.md) |
| Enforcement outside the model at the tool boundary | RW24, RW23, AgentSecBench (RW08), NetInjectBench (RW09) | The design approach of the defended system; the field's current consensus, not a TrustBench idea | [`related-work.md`](related-work.md) |
| Attack wordings and the paired benchmark idea | AgentDojo (RW01), InjecAgent (RW02) | Attack renderings on TrustBench's own synthetic workflows | [`docs/holdout-run.md`](../docs/holdout-run.md) |
| Prompt-level and detection defenses | Spotlighting (RW10), repeat user prompt (RW11), MELON (RW17) | Re-implemented from their papers and AgentDojo source, measured on the same harness; not the authors' systems | [`docs/defense-comparison.md`](../docs/defense-comparison.md) |
| Separate attacker-goal and unsafe-effect endpoints | WASP (RW04) | Both endpoints reported from committed tool state | [`docs/security-utility.md`](../docs/security-utility.md) |

## Engineering contributions (claimed, with evidence)

What the project can claim is evaluation and engineering practice. Each item is a working, tested artifact, not a research
finding.

| Contribution | What it is | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paired, preregistered evaluation on sealed holdouts | Both arms on identical inputs and seeds; holdouts sealed by hash, run once; invalid runs listed, never counted as secure; amendments recorded before the results they govern | [`protocol/preregister.md`](../protocol/preregister.md), [`protocol/amendments.md`](../protocol/amendments.md) |
| Outcomes from committed tool state | The evaluator reads what the tools committed, not the model's reply; audited against blind AI reviewers | [`label-audit.md`](label-audit.md) |
| Same-harness comparison | The frozen system, the capability gateway alone and re-implemented published defenses run on one harness with one baseline | [`docs/defense-comparison.md`](../docs/defense-comparison.md) |
| Regression release gate | Blocks verdict regressions and a more permissive policy audit trail on every push; injected regressions are tested to fail it | [`docs/release-gate.md`](../docs/release-gate.md) |
| Fault, restart and rollback drills | Measured recovery for provider hangs, read-only storage, restarts, policy and image rollback | [`reports/fault-drill.md`](../reports/fault-drill.md), [`reports/rollback-drill.md`](../reports/rollback-drill.md) |
| Offline reproducibility package | Rebuilds every published number from committed raw run records in a clean container | [`repro/README.md`](../repro/README.md) |
| Claim-to-artifact ledger | Every number in the report and in this register is resolved from a committed file and hash-pinned | [`report-claims.json`](report-claims.json) |
| Live test service | The comparison can be rerun from a browser or the CLI with no setup or with a visitor's own free-tier key | [`docs/live-service.md`](../docs/live-service.md) |

The directive-flow check, signed provenance envelope and sticky denials are implemented and tested, but they are a
specific combination of known ideas (above), and their measured contribution on development data is not separated from
zero. They are listed as engineering, not as a new defense.

## Hypotheses that need more evidence

| Hypothesis | Current evidence | What would test it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The provenance-aware layer, not capability scoping, causes the improvement | Development ablation not separated from zero ({{abl:comparisons[id=directive_flow_on_gateway].results.unsafe_committed_effect.point|pp}}, {{abl:comparisons[id=directive_flow_on_gateway].results.unsafe_committed_effect.cluster_bootstrap95|ci}}); no confirmatory capability-only arm | A preregistered holdout with a capability-only arm |
| The effect holds on holdout-1 on its own | {{h:per_holdout[analysis=holdout1/agentdojo_important_instructions].verdict|raw}} ({{h:per_holdout[analysis=holdout1/agentdojo_important_instructions].unsafe_committed_effect.ci95_pp|civ}}) | More holdout tasks or repetitions |
| The defense holds against an adaptive attacker | Not tested; AutoDojo (RW07) shows static benchmarks can overstate efficacy | An adaptive black-box or optimisation-based attack on the gateway |
| The effect generalises to other models, workflows and attack families | One confirmatory model; on new attack families the interval includes zero | Further preregistered holdouts |
| The defense does not over-block helpful third-party instructions | No such tasks (AgentDyn, RW06) | Tasks with legitimate instructions in content |
| The evaluator's labels match human judgement | AI reviewers only | A human review of the same blind packets |

## Not claimed

- **Novelty.** Combining capability scoping, approvals and provenance labels is not new (RW19, RW20, RW21, RW22, RW24). No
  new defense idea is claimed.
- **Security guarantee.** No formal or universal guarantee. Results are measured rates with intervals for one configuration;
  zero observed failures would still not mean zero risk.
- **The "novel candidate" label.** The directive-flow systems carry the working label "ours (novel candidate …)" in
  `configs/defenses.yaml`, the generated [`docs/defense-comparison.md`](../docs/defense-comparison.md) and the recorded run
  reports. It was a working name given before the prior-work review (TB-043), not a claim. It stays because the live
  configuration must match the frozen copy byte for byte (A-023; `scripts/verify-frozen.py`) and recorded reports are never
  rewritten; changing it needs a new amendment and selection.
- **Production readiness.** Synthetic data and local mock tools only.
- **Patentability or publication.** Neither is claimed or implied; both would need specialist review.
- **Hiring outcomes.** Portfolio material may use only the statements in "Measured results that may be stated", with their
  qualifiers; no ranking, percentile or hiring claims. `scripts/check-claims.py` checks any file under `portfolio/` against
  this register's numbers.
